subject: Connectivity decision: peering vs PrivateLink vs S2S VPN for EdgeCorp private deployment
messages:
From: Tom Harris <tharris@edgecorp.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Connectivity options for Greenwood pilot (peering / PrivateLink / VPN)

Hi Soojin / Marissa —

Quick intro: EdgeCorp is moving forward with the Greenwood pilot and networking is the main gating item. Our infra team wants a clear recommendation from Redwood on which connectivity pattern to use for Redwood Private: VPC Peering, PrivateLink (interface endpoints), or a managed site-to-site VPN from our DCs to Redwood-hosted VPCs. We need an answer we can present to our security and procurement folks next Tuesday.

Pointers from EdgeCorp constraints:
- Data plane must not traverse the public internet at rest (no direct public IPs).
- We prefer minimal changes to our existing firewall/NAT setup (we’re somewhat locked-down).
- Latency SLA target: p95 < 40ms for inference requests from our primary DC.
- We may use multiple regions later but will start with a single us-west-2 deployment.

Specific asks:
1) Recommend a primary connectivity pattern and a fallback.
2) List measurable trade-offs (latency, bandwidth costs, operational complexity, cross-account IAM surface).
3) Any blockers for Private deployments with our compliance needs (audit logs, KMS routing).

Thanks — Tom

--
Tom Harris

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Connectivity options for Greenwood pilot (peering / PrivateLink / VPN)

Tom —

Thanks for the clear summary. High level recommendation up front: 1) For a single-region, low-latency requirement, start with VPC Peering (cross-account peering) where possible; 2) Use PrivateLink (interface endpoints) when you need tight IAM separation and explicit endpoint controls (best for per-service authorization and easier egress controls); 3) Reserve S2S VPN as a fallback/bridge for on-premises environments where you cannot establish peering or want a simple encrypted tunnel quickly.

Short trade-off bullets:
- Latency: Peering ≈ lowest latency (L2-ish within cloud fabric), PrivateLink adds ~2–6ms overhead typical, S2S VPN varies widely (20–100ms depending on path & NAT).
- Throughput: Peering supports high throughput native to VPC; PrivateLink throughput per ENI is limited (requires scaling endpoints); VPN throughput depends on gateway sizing and can be bursty.
- Cost: Peering — regional data transfer fees (cross-AZ/region), PrivateLink — per-hour endpoint + per-GB processed, VPN — per-hour gateway + data charges; for long-lived, high-bandwidth peering often cheaper.
- Security/Surface: PrivateLink reduces cross-account routing surface (only endpoint ENIs exposed) and helps restrict access to specific services. Peering exposes full routing between VPCs unless you implement strict security groups/NACLs. VPN keeps traffic encapsulated but relies on customer gateway CVM and key rotation discipline.

Compliance notes: We can integrate audit logs and KMS either way, but Private requires more careful KMS key policy design if the endpoint initiates encryption contexts. For SOC2 concerns, peering + VPC flow logs shipped to a central logging account meets requirements if both sides agree on retention.

I’ll attach a short matrix and run a quick latency test plan. Ben, can you add any infra-specific caveats (route propagation, TGW impact, cross-account role needs) and a proposed test schedule?

Next steps:
- Ben to share an analysis + test plan.
- EdgeCorp to confirm whether they can accept cross-account peering.
- If peering is blocked, we pivot to PrivateLink with an endpoint autoscaling plan.

Regards,

Soojin
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
soojin_lee@redwood.com
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Connectivity options for Greenwood pilot (peering / PrivateLink / VPN)

Adding the infra details Tom asked for + quick experiment results. Attachment: connectivity-analysis.xlsx (summary) and latency-tests.csv (raw measurements). Also included a draw.io topology (topology-draft.drawio).

Key infra caveats / findings:
- Cross-account VPC Peering: Requires creating peering request from EdgeCorp account to our Redwood Private account. Route table entries must be limited to subnets running inference; default route propagation via TGW can accidentally widen access — recommend avoiding automated TGW prop until after canary.
- PrivateLink (interface endpoints): For heavy throughput (inference serving), endpoint scaling is necessary. Each ENI supports a limited number of flows; on GCP/Azure similar patterns apply but specifics differ. We recommend an endpoint autoscaler + warm pool.
- VPN: Fastest to bootstrap (30–60m) but adds jitter and NAT issues. Our early lab VPN tests to an on-prem PoP showed p95 ~ 48ms and occasional spikes to 200ms under NATed egress.
- Egress/IPs / Firewalls: If EdgeCorp is strict about egress IPs, peering avoids NAT egress changes. PrivateLink requires you to allow AWS-managed endpoint ENI IPs in security lists. VPN will originate from your gateway/CR- devices so firewall rules are straightforward.
- IAM/Service Access: PrivateLink gives per-service IAM bindings (good for least privilege). For peering we surface fewer IAM controls but more network-level blast radius — use restrictive security groups and per-subnet route tables.

Proposed test plan (high level):
1) Week 1: Create a staging peering connection, run p95 latency tests (ICMP + TCP + tokenized inference RPC).
2) Week 2: Create PrivateLink endpoint in our VPC, deploy endpoint autoscaler, run throughput ramp tests and per-request latency.
3) Week 3: If peering blocked, spin up managed VPN and run long-run stability tests (48h).

Operational recommendations:
- Default to peering when EdgeCorp allows cross-account peering and you need best latency/throughput.
- If security/compliance strictly forbids routing, choose PrivateLink and set up endpoint autoscaling and stricter KMS scoping.
- Always validate with a 48h soak test and implement flow logs + alerting on error-rate/latency regressions.

Ben

ben_carter@redwood.com

Tom —

Thanks for the context and Ben/Soojin for the thorough analysis. Decision for the pilot: proceed with cross-account VPC Peering as the primary path (EdgeCorp confirmed peering is acceptable), with a PrivateLink path defined as a controlled fallback. Ben will own the staging peering and test run; Soojin will own the runbook updates and compliance checklist.

Deliverables & timeline:
- By 2028-06-14: Staging peering established + 48h soak test (Ben)
- By 2028-06-16: PrivateLink blueprint (with autoscaler settings) and KMS policy draft (Soojin)
- By 2028-06-20: Exec summary for procurement showing cost delta peering vs PrivateLink (Marissa)

Tom, if you can confirm your team's point-of-contact for peering creation (account IDs and VPC IDs), we’ll get started Monday.

Marissa Cole
Principal Product Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
